itemized_evaluation.justification: The paper includes explicit conflict of interest and funding disclosures in 'Notes on the record': 'Competing interests: D.S. is the founder and a beneficiary of FreshCredit Inc. and the founder of The FreshCredit Lab. FreshCredit Inc holds granted US utility patents... Funding: none received; independent research.'

The paper is an un-reviewed preprint with pending/incomplete repository deposits: 'DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/TBD' and 'The Supporting Document and Technical Appendix are in preparation (see collection index); until they are deposited, the frozen-criteria and protocol claims that cite them are self-attested.'

Prior works and vendor statistics are rigorously audited and represented without selective framing. For example, in §1.1: 'A widely circulated claim that “95% of synthetic identities pass onboarding undetected,” attributed to Thomson Reuters across vendor blogs, has no locatable primary source, methodology, or date; we treat it as an unverifiable industry statistic and do not rely on it.' Also in §1.1: 'Experimental demand characteristics show heterogeneous, bidirectional participation effects with frequent nulls — 12 of 19 studies positive, 5 clear nulls; the review concludes little is securely known about conditions, mechanisms, or magnitudes.'

The methodology establishes a bit-identical reproducible simulation protocol and cites external system confirmations: 'All criteria were pre-registered in code; all reported runs are bit-identical under re-execution' (§3.7), providing exact random seeds (e.g., 'seed 42', 'seed 20260905', 'seed 20260907') and parameterization throughout.

Sampling and measurement biases in the simulations are explicitly identified, tested, and controlled for. In §3.6: 'A half-circle phase-initialization map... inflates the K = 0 “incoherent control” to R = 0.635 ± 0.014 (200-seed ensemble) — an artifact that would report strong coherence in a fully uncoupled population. The full-circle stereographic map gives R = 0.040 ± 0.021 at K = 0, at the finite-size floor...'. In §3.7: 'The pre-registered hypothesis — bilateral validation is symmetric, surveillance is not — survives a bias-corrected estimator; the uncorrected estimator inverts the result'.

Sample sizes and simulation horizons are explicitly justified against finite-size floors and statistical power requirements. In §3.6: 'N = 500... at the finite-size floor 1/sqrt(500) ≈ 0.045', '200-seed ensemble', and in §3.6 Sim P4b: 'A lower-powered seeding — single offer per category, chain-rule estimate for trust_signal — gives p = 0.109 (not significant); the null is preserved in the record...'. In §4: 'exact OU discretization, 64 parallel chains, >= 30 autocorrelation times per run'.

While proper controls are used in the simulations (e.g., isolated control K = 0 in Sim P1, zero-knowledge-observation control in Sim-OBS), double-blinding is neither implemented nor explicitly justified as impossible in the text.

Appropriate non-parametric permutation tests, surrogate-corrected transfer entropy, and regression models are paired with explicit effect sizes and practical significance evaluations. In §3.6 Sim P4b: 'energy distance 0.00021, permutation p = 0.005 (2,000 permutations) against the pre-registered p < 0.05... an energy distance of 0.00021 is practically negligible at the tested scale, so “heterogeneity matters for terminal outcomes” is supported only in the statistical sense, not in the effect-size sense'.

Randomization seeds, agent distributions, and network topologies are exhaustively detailed. For example, in §3.6 Sim P1c: 'seed 42... N = 500, omega ~ Cauchy(0,1), stereographic initialization, Euler dt = 0.05, burn-in 100 t.u. + measurement 200 t.u., 2 graph realizations x 2 seeds per topology — with the coupling degree-normalized (K/k_i...) on Erdos-Renyi (p in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5}...), Barabasi-Albert (m = 12 and m = 2...)'. In §3.7 Sim P7: 'present-biased agents (beta ~ U(0.4, 0.9), delta ~ U(0.95, 0.999), horizons 6–24 steps)'.

Standard deviations, 95% confidence intervals, and exact p-values are consistently reported across the paper: e.g., §3.2 ('-43.7%/year (95% CI [-44.2, -43.2]; R^2 = 0.984)'), §3.6 ('R = 0.739 ± 0.029', 'p = 0.005', 'p = 0.109'), and §3.7 ('agent->validator 0.0315 ± 0.003 bits, validator->agent 0.0283 ± 0.002 bits — 95% CIs across 8 replicas', 'permutation p = 0.004').

Raw numbers, baseline figures, and absolute risks are explicitly provided alongside relative percentages. In §3.6 Sim P2: 'compromises 100% of records; a breach under database-per-tenant isolation compromises exactly the breached tenants (0.2% at N = 500) — a 99.8% relative reduction in conditional exposure'. In §3.9: 'N_all = 3 x 10^8 records... Centralized expected exposure at p_org = 0.05: 15M records/yr... Per-tenant wins ~8x in the favorable region — p_device = 0.005, p_commonmode = 0.001 -> E_T = 1.8M vs. 15M — and loses when endpoint multiplication dominates: p_device = 0.06 -> E_T = 18.3M > 15M'. In §3.6 Sim P3: 'marginal cost per additional user is constant ($0.001/event)... $1–$100 of settlement per decision'.

Excluded data points, failed runs, and estimator defects are fully logged and accounted for. In §3.2: 'A -31.6%/year fit on a small subsample (df = 7) is unreconstructable from the cited series — its 1980 anchor of “roughly $20,000/GB” conflicts with the sourced Komorowski 1980 rows ($152K–$700K/GB) — and is not used'. In §3.7: 'Two audit-trail entries record corrections to the measurement, not the model: the initial P5 transfer-entropy estimator (8 bins, 600 steps) carried a finite-sample bias... Both artifacts and their corrections are documented in §Q. The stack’s rule applies here unchanged: nulls and failed estimators stay in the record next to the successes.' In §4: 'The first-run estimator defect (an ad-hoc estimator producing symmetric garbage) was caught by the frozen criteria, archived, and disclosed with the run record.'

The paper strictly maintains outcome metric consistency and explicitly warns against swapping or conflating surrogate simulation metrics with real-world deployment outcomes. In §1.5: 'No achieved end-to-end performance is claimed for deployed applications of the protocol. Claims carry the stack’s epistemic labels...'. In §3.6: 'In the current ABM the phase layer is decoupled from the master-law layer: every R reported below is a Kuramoto result on stereographically initialized phases with natural frequencies omega_k that have no trust-theoretic counterpart... coupling the two layers is registered future work.' In §3.7 Sim P6: 'A DebtRank-style cascade is not applied to data custody, for two reasons. (i) Category error...'

The distinction between statistical significance and practical impact is explicitly enforced. In §3.6 Sim P4b: 'the terminal trust-vector distribution of the heterogeneous population is statistically distinguishable from the homogeneous reference: energy distance 0.00021, permutation p = 0.005 (2,000 permutations) against the pre-registered p < 0.05... What the result actually shows is narrower than the old headline: the seeding variable is not inert... but an energy distance of 0.00021 is practically negligible at the tested scale, so “heterogeneity matters for terminal outcomes” is supported only in the statistical sense, not in the effect-size sense'.

Confounding variables, demand characteristics, and definitional artifacts are explicitly separated from causal claims. In §3.6 Sim P1b: 'Definitional component: component (i) of the leakage operationalization (K_eff = K(1-l)) makes part of the R-decay definitional — Kuramoto coherence decreases monotonically in coupling by construction; the non-definitional content is component (ii) (observation noise)...'. In §3.4: 'headline x402 volume figures are inflated by late-2025 memecoin activity — the PING mint spike and retry/test traffic — but the claim here rests on demonstrated sub-cent settlement cost'. Demand characteristics and observer effects are the core subject of §4.

Figures and their captions explicitly document baselines, floors, error bands, and un-distorted axes (e.g., Figure 4: 'at the 1/sqrt(N) ≈ 0.045 finite-size floor... and the phase-map-control side panel'; Figure 10: 'with the 0.01-bit detection floor marked; every replica lands on the correct side of the floor in both architectures. Magnitudes are floor-adjacent, so no ratio headline is reported'; Figure 5: 'Phase arrows are seeded schematic draws; only the printed re-run values are measured').

Hypotheses and pass/fail criteria were pre-specified in code prior to runs, and post-hoc threshold switching is explicitly rejected even when tests fail. In §4 (Sim-OBS): 'pre-registered with frozen pass/fail criteria before any data contact... Result: compound FAIL... An instrument-recalibration pass (regression-initialized EM) did not move any criterion across its frozen threshold, and no threshold was adjusted post hoc. The verdict is reported as FAIL'. See also §1.4 ('The hypothesis below matches the tested design (§3.6) and is the registered form') and §3.6 ('honest null on the quantitative threshold').

Long-run temporal validity, cold-start traps, and multi-year attack horizons are explicitly modeled and evaluated in §3.10 ('Temporal validity: cold start and long-run dynamics... 10^5 events... 563/144/140/120/72/24 days') and §3.7 Sim P8 ('1.4-year figure applies to manufacturing HIGH standing (10 units, 1,005 events) at a conservative reference rate of 2/day (at 0.5/day, 5.5 years)').

The paper explicitly rejects linear extrapolations beyond measured bounds and splits regression models across eras when trends change. In §3.4: 'ordinary peer-to-peer transfers peaked at 10,920 TPS on 15 cores in the controlled November 26, 2024 Parity test, and the often-quoted 623,230 TPS figure is Parity’s linear extrapolation to 100 cores, not a measurement'. In §3.2: 'the cost curve is measured, not asserted, and the trend is era-split (Figure 3): a re-fit on the full sourced Komorowski table (273 transcribed drive-price points, 1980–2009) gives a log-linear decline of -43.7%/year... while the modern era is much flatter — fleet endpoints give ≈ -14%/year over 2009–2022... with the caveat that the 2025–26 NAND shortage reversed SSD pricing (enterprise +257%) while HDDs continued the trend (+35%) — a 46-year pattern, not a law'.

Mathematical models and results strictly adhere to mathematical boundaries and domain reality. For example, in §3.3: 'where the trust index iota(T) = tanh(w * T_tilde) in (-1, 1) distorts outcome probabilities by a bounded exponential tilt... the distortion is bounded (|log P_tilde/P| <= 2*gamma*max|u_hat|...)'. In §3.10: 'The leak-free symmetric limit (theory preset) accumulates unbounded values under a stationary honest stream (S = 249 after 10^5 events)... The baseline-restoring form (delta_S > 0, S_base the no-information prior — the protocol/biological presets) avoids both pathologies: bounded recovery after shocks'.
